title: Host Exchange Orchestrator with SLO-backed Capacity Leases
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Design and implement a Host Exchange Orchestrator: a fleet-side agent and controller that issues time-bound capacity leases to services, coordinates host handoffs during upgrades/drains, and enforces SLO-preserving constraints. Goal: enable safe host rotation/upgrades and planned maintenance without manual leak of capacity or tail SLO regressions for Dedicated customers. This ticket covers design, controller prototype, console control surface for occupancy windows, and metrics/alerting required for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can assign and revoke capacity leases to route groups with explicit throughput contracts
When a host is marked for replacement, the orchestrator sequences evacuations respecting active leases and observed KV-cache warmup status
KV-cache prewarm API integrated so warm hosts are preferred for handoffs; cold-host traffic cap enforced until warm threshold met
Console exposes per-fleet occupancy windows, lease durations, and an emergency 'hold' that pauses new evacuations
Automated canary upgrade: 5% of fleet rotated with no >3% SLO degradation in 30m window under synthetic load
Rollout runbook documented and tested in staging (playbook with rollback triggers and mitigations)
technical_notes: Capacity lease model: leases = (throughput_units, expires_at, priority_tier, token). Controller persists leases to etcd and emits events for agents
Handoff algorithm: select target hosts with available lease headroom, prefer hosts with warm KV-cache and compatible kernel selection; fallback to staging hosts with transient throttle
Soft-fence semantics: hosts entering maintenance get a soft-fence tag preventing new long-lived requests; existing requests up to grace-window finish
Prewarm signal: agent exposes KV-cache filled ratio and estimated warm ETA. Controller uses a configurable threshold (default 0.7) before allowing full traffic transfer
Eviction safety limiter: do not reduce fleet effective throughput below SLO_budget_margin (configurable; default 10%) while upgrades in flight
Metrics: capacity_leases.active, lease_revocations.total, kv_warm_ratio[host], handoff.latency.p50/p95, slo_error_rate_by_fleet, maintenance_blocked_count
Failure modes: inability to find warm targets => throttle evacuations and surface backpressure; agent-connection loss => mark host quarantined and reassign leases after lease-expiry grace
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Lease duration tradeoff: shorter leases increase controller churn but reduce tail risk for long-held reservations; default 30m chosen as balance
Strong consistency vs eventual: store leases in strongly-consistent store (etcd) to avoid double-assignment at the cost of slightly higher latency on lease ops
Prewarm accuracy: we accept heuristic estimate for KV warm percent rather than exact byte-level correctness to reduce agent overhead
Grace period length: 120s for in-flight requests chosen after benchmarking ML inference tail distributions in staging
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit + integration tests; design doc and console mockups reviewed by SRE and Product
Phase 1: controller prototype in canary fleet (non-customer-facing) with synthetic traffic; validate metrics and eviction protections
Phase 2: enable orchestrator for an internal Dedicated customer’s staging fleet; run full upgrade simulation and game-day
Phase 3: gated release to 10% of production fleets with automated rollback on SLO regressions
Phase 4: gradual ramp to full fleet; monitor for 72h after each 10% increase and run audit log review
qa_and_testing_notes: Test harness to simulate mixed request distributions (short chat completions + long-context generations)
Inject delayed KV-warm signals and ensure controller throttles handoffs appropriately
Chaos tests: kill agents during handoff; verify leases reassign after expiry without double-serve
Load tests to validate SLO_budget_margin protects throughput under concurrent upgrades
console_requirements: UI panel to set occupancy windows (start/end) per fleet and per region
Lease inspector view: list active leases, owner route-group, expires_at, and priority
One-click pause/resume maintenance button with audit log entry
Alerting rules template creators can attach to lease_revocations and slo_error_rate_by_fleet
security_and_compliance_notes: Lease tokens rotated regularly and encrypted in transit and at rest via KMS
Audit log entries for lease create/revoke tied to customer tenancy context
No customer data persisted in controller beyond opaque tenant ids and lease metadata
